  - heading "Practical observations and exam-style report" [level=2]
  - list:
    - listitem: Predict how the water level changes. Record V1 with the solid clear above the vessel.
    - listitem: Lower slowly and pause during partial immersion. Record V2, captured overflow and whether the whole solid is underwater.
    - listitem: At the immersed hold, keep the solid clear of the base and walls. Record both readings and any collected overflow.
    - listitem: Apply immersed volume = V2 − V1 + captured overflow. Only use it as full solid volume when fully submerged.
    - listitem: Lift clear and record again. Check that vessel water plus captured water still equals the starting water.
    - listitem: Repeat fresh overflow and specimen controls. Write a result, explain why partial immersion or lost overflow gives an incorrect full-volume result, and state a limitation.
  - text: Prediction
  - textbox "Displacement prediction": The water reading should rise as the solid enters. A partial immersion gives only immersed volume. With full immersion, the rise plus any collected overflow should equal the whole solid volume. Overflow should stay collected after lifting.

  - generic "Worked displacement, overflow and force substitutions"
  - text: Result, conclusion and limitation
  - textbox "Displacement conclusion"
  - paragraph: Force calculations are a teacher extension. Reference geometry, densities and slow motion are idealized. No bubbles, absorption, meniscus, wetting film, splash, drag, suspension volume or drainage transit inventory is solved. Overflow is assigned directly to its receiver. Meshes approximate the analytic curved surfaces; computed readings do not represent calibrated instrument precision. Eye-level inspection is a horizontal camera preset, not a parallax-error solver. The latest 60 observations remain in this browser.
